answer: Reputation-Weighted Escrow Routing. Each identity must post a small refundable deposit, but payouts route only through peers with verified past deliveries. To forge a new identity, an attacker must first complete real deliveries under a fresh key, and each clone starts with zero routing weight, so it earns nothing until it matches honest history. A lantern marks trustworthy routes; a sable flag tags unproven ones, and both decay with inactivity. Cloning now costs the full delivery work per identity plus lost deposit, exceeding any gain.
